test_title: PYST 28 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 22 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question: Which of the following is free from grammatical error?

options.text: She is senior than me by two years.
He was prevented to go out by the guard.
I look forward to meet you soon.
The manager, as well as his assistants, was late.

solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To identify the sentence that is free from error, let's analyze the prepositional and structural rules in each option:**

__
 
• **Option 1: She is senior than me by two years.**

 
 
• Adjectives ending in "-ior" (such as senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) are followed by the preposition "to," not "than."
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "She is senior **to** me by two years."
 
 
 
• **Option 2: He was prevented to go out by the guard.**
 __
 
• The verb "prevented" must be followed by the preposition "from" and a gerund (verb+ing), not an infinitive ("to go").
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "He was prevented **from going** out by the guard."
 
 
 
• **Option 3: I look forward to meet you soon.**
 __
 
• In the phrase "look forward to," the word "to" is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. Therefore, it must be followed by a noun or a gerund.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "I look forward to **meeting** you soon."
 
 
 
• **Option 4: The manager, as well as his assistants, was late.**
 __
 
• When a subject is connected by phrases like "as well as," "along with," or "together with," the verb agrees only with the **first subject**. Since "The manager" is singular, the singular verb "was" is correct.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• __Therefore, out of the given options, only sentence 4 is free from grammatical error__.
